usage.notes: Use GTEx open-access data as a population reference for tissue-specific gene expression/regulation and targeted educational queries. Prefer release-pinned summary data or targeted API calls instead of sending large expression matrices to the browser. Protected raw sequence data and full donor metadata are a separate controlled-access class and must never be fetched by the public web application. GTEx tissue distributions are cohort reference context, not an individual's normal range or diagnosis.

license.identifier: GTEx Portal acknowledgement/publication policy plus NIH genomic-data access terms
license.scope: The GTEx Portal provides open-access summary/derived datasets and states that GTEx data, visualizations and tools can be used with acknowledgement. Raw sequence data and full donor metadata are protected access and governed by NIH/dbGaP controlled-access requirements. Panacea must verify the exact release/file terms and any third-party annotation licenses before commercial redistribution or bundling.
license.notes: Preserve GTEx acknowledgement, release and dbGaP accession where applicable. Open access does not authorize re-identification attempts or relaxation of privacy obligations. Controlled-access data use must follow the approved Data Use Certification, consent limitations and current NIH security requirements.

validation.notes: GTEx is a high-value research reference from non-diseased tissue samples, but donor composition, post-mortem collection, tissue heterogeneity, processing pipelines and cohort size affect distributions. Expression/QTL results must not be presented as patient-specific expression, disease status, treatment response or a universal normal interval.

provenance.notes: Persist GTEx project (Adult/dGTEx/NHP-dGTEx where applicable), analysis release, dbGaP accession/version when supplied, tissue ontology/name, GENCODE/annotation release, gene/transcript stable ID and version, expression unit/normalization method, QTL type and variant/gene identifiers, sample-count/summary context, source file or API endpoint, retrieval date and Panacea adapter version. Never combine V8/V10/V11 values or different annotation releases without explicit harmonization and provenance.

adapter.notes: Planned open-data flow: gene/tissue/reference query -> explicit GTEx analysis release -> targeted Portal/API or approved open-access snapshot -> validate gene/transcript IDs, tissue and units -> normalize population summaries/QTLs to PanaceaTissueExpressionReference -> retain release, sample context and acknowledgement. Protected-access flow is intentionally excluded from the public web adapter and would require a separately approved research environment. Do not translate cohort percentiles into individual abnormal/normal labels.

trust.notes: Highly authoritative tissue-expression/QTL reference with reproducible release-pinned datasets. Clinical applicability is limited by cohort and tissue context, while rights/privacy requirements differ between open summary data and protected individual-level genomic data.
